stories.title: As the facilitator running a voice pilot, I want to list and replay a participant's recorded audio through the control API, with every play audited before any audio leaves, so that a disputed line can be checked without the audio leaking.

acs.text: each audio folder records its session: the speech worker writes `<AUDIO_DIR>/<logIdentity>/session.json` `{ v: 1, sessionId }` (0600, temp file, rename, directory fsync, no link followed) once, before the first WAV of the process, and never for a skipped or refused segment or a guard stop; a marker failure stops the store with `write_error` (TC-0219) ; ticked 2026-11-12: speech store/session-marker.test.ts and audio-store.test.ts (`AudioStore: session marker`: written before the first WAV, not rewritten, none when nothing is written, `write_error` at each of the four file steps, a planted link never followed)

control hands the session id to the worker: `SPEECH_SESSION_ID` is set by `buildSpeechEnv` from `extra` only (never inherited, never on the allowlist), the worker requires a valid one (`isValidSessionId`) whenever the store is configured, and a bad value is a config error naming the variable only (TC-0220) ; ticked 2026-11-12: speech config.test.ts (`test_store_needs_a_valid_session_id`), control speech-env.test.ts (`SPEECH_SESSION_ID`: from `extra` only, never inherited, invalid omitted) and voice-host.test.ts

`AuditLog.append` reports success: it returns `Promise<boolean>` (true on success, false on every failure path, still never rejecting) and accepts `audio.played { role, segment, by }`, with every line rebuilt field by field so no extra key is written (TC-0221) ; ticked 2026-11-12: control audit-log.test.ts (`AuditLog.append reports success; audio.played`: true on success, false on every failure path, exact `audio.played` shape, older events unchanged)

`AudioCatalog.find(sessionId)` returns every identity whose marker names the session by scanning the audio directory on every request (markers read `O_NOFOLLOW`, at most 4 KB); a marker that is missing, torn, a link, of another `v` or naming another session is ignored (TC-0222) ; ticked 2026-11-12: control audio-catalog.test.ts (`AudioCatalog.find by marker`, the root-mode cases of ruling R3, the fallback cases)

listing: `GET /sessions/:id/audio` returns the identities, `recordingStopped` and each segment with `audio: available | deleted | missing` and never `raw`, over the index files of every identity (64 MiB cap, torn lines skipped); a folder recorded before the marker existed is found through the session log's `logIdentity`; a session with no audio is 404 (TC-0223) ; ticked 2026-11-12: control audio-catalog.test.ts (`AudioCatalog.list`, `find fallback`, `readSegmentIndex`), log-identity.test.ts, audio-routes.test.ts (the listing) and audio-replay.e2e.test.ts; `available` means only that the WAV opens as a regular own file with one link

safe whole-file read: a segment's WAV is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` under real directories of this user, judged on the descriptor (regular file, own uid, `nlink` 1, 44 to 524288 bytes), read whole, required to have an index line that is not marked deleted, and only then is `audio.played` appended; a failed audit returns `audit_unavailable` with no bytes (TC-0224) ; ticked 2026-11-12: control audio-replay.test.ts (whole read, audit after the read and before the bytes, `audit_unavailable`, every refusal, the race cases)

HTTP routes: `GET /sessions/:id/audio` and `GET /sessions/:id/audio/:role/:segment` answer 200 with the whole file (`Accept-Ranges: none`, any `Range` ignored, exact `Content-Length`, `no-store`, `nosniff`), 400 for a missing or bad `X-Acr-By`, 401 before any file call, 404, 410 `audio_deleted`, 503 `audit_unavailable` (no audio; a JSON body with only the code) or `busy` (at most 8 in flight); nothing logs a path, id or name (TC-0225) ; ticked 2026-11-12: control audio-routes.test.ts (200 headers, `Range` ignored, 400, 401, 404, 410, 503 `audit_unavailable` and `busy`, `X-Acr-By` on both routes)

a real store and a real control API work end to end (list, replay, one `audio.played` line with no content keys, two identities for one session, 404 after the sweep, routes alive with `VOICE_ENABLED=0`), and mutation checks (the plan named five: audit after the bytes, no `nlink` check, no index-line requirement, audit result ignored, any `by` accepted; eleven were run, adding `Range` honoured, the deleted-mark checks, the token check, the fallback ignoring a marker and two wiring mutations) each fail a named test and are reverted (TC-0226) ; ticked 2026-11-12: control audio-replay.e2e.test.ts (real store, real API, real sweep; two identities; `VOICE_ENABLED=0`) and eleven mutation checks from the Task 8 report, each failing a named test and reverted (prior evidence, not re-run)

stories.title: As the facilitator running a voice pilot, I want to delete what a participant said (the whole session, one role or one participant) through the control API, with every deletion audited before anything is removed, so that a participant's request to have their audio erased can be honoured with proof.

acs.text: the `deleted` index line has one definition: `@acr/speech/protocol` exports `DeletedIndexLine`, `isDeletedLine` (`v` 1, `kind` `deleted`, file-safe `segment`, 16 lower-case hex `op`, finite non-negative `ts`) and `appendDeletedLines` (O_APPEND, O_NOFOLLOW, no O_CREAT, one descriptor judged on its `fstat` as a regular file of this user, a torn last line terminated first, all lines in one write and one fsync, a short write continued, errors carry the errno code only); speech's `readIndex` skips the line; `protocol.ts` may import only zod, `@acr/events` and `node:fs` (TC-0233); ticked 2026-11-13: speech protocol-deleted-line.test.ts (the guard, `appendDeletedLines`: one write, torn line, link, non-regular, foreign owner, no create, short write, no path in a message), imports.test.ts (only zod, `@acr/events`, `node:fs`) and store/index-file.test.ts (`readIndex` skips the line); the one-fsync count is not asserted (no seam), the one-write count is

route: `DELETE /sessions/:id/audio` behind the service token (401 before any file call, 404 on a bad session id or no audio) takes a strict body `{ scope, reason, by }` (scope session, role or participant; reason `facilitator` or `participant_request`; `by` required in the `<name>-console` form, `X-Acr-By` when present must equal it; unknown keys 400) and covers every role and identity the scope names; at most 4 deletes in flight (503 `busy`) (TC-0234); ticked 2026-11-13: control audio-routes.test.ts (`DELETE /sessions/:id/audio: refusals before any file call`: 401, 404, the strict body table, `X-Acr-By` differing; `outcomes`: the session and participant scopes over HTTP; the cap of 4 and its own counter) and audio-delete.test.ts (`deleteAudio: scopes`: session, role and participant); an oversize body is 413 `payload_too_large` like every other body route, with the connection closed, no file call and no audit line (audio-routes.test.ts: `a body over 4096 bytes with a declared Content-Length is 413 payload_too_large` and `a streamed (chunked, undeclared) body over 4096 bytes is 413 payload_too_large`)

live refusal: delete answers 409 `session_live` with nothing written when VoiceHost holds a live entry for the session (worker, restart backoff, `mediaLost`, probe) or the store lock is held by another process, checked before any file call and again per identity (TC-0235); ticked 2026-11-13: control audio-delete.test.ts (`deleteAudio: live`), audio-routes.test.ts (409 before the catalog, a throwing predicate), voice-host.test.ts and livekit-outage.test.ts (`isLive`: worker, backoff, `mediaLost`, probe) and audio-delete.e2e.test.ts (live with no audio folder, live between identities, a real second process holding the store lock)

audit first: per identity, under the in-process mutex and the store lock (re-checking the marker under the lock), `audio.deleted { scope, reason, by, segments, op }` is appended BEFORE any index line or unlink and fails closed (that identity is `pending` with `audit_unavailable`, nothing marked or unlinked); then the `deleted` lines go in one write with one fsync, then each WAV is unlinked through a checked descriptor; a `participant_request` with no audio still writes one `segments: 0` line (TC-0236); ticked 2026-11-13: control audio-delete.test.ts (`the audit comes first`: the audit sees every index and WAV untouched; a false audit; `segments: 0`; `store_unsafe`; `a lock lost between the marks and the unlinks`; the files cases: torn line, link, `nlink` 2, one write) and audio-delete.e2e.test.ts (an audit that cannot be written; the crash after the audit leaves the audio playable, a retry writes a new op)

partial results: identities are processed one at a time in sorted order and never under several locks; under the lock each identity is re-checked: one that provably no longer belongs to the session (its folder missing, or its marker naming another session) is listed in `gone`, and one whose root or folder cannot be re-checked (an unsafe root, the folder swapped for a link, a file or another user's folder) is `pending store_unsafe`, never `gone`; 200 `{ deleted, gone, identities, pending: [] }` when all are done, otherwise 503 with the same body and the worst reason as the code (`store_unsafe` over `audit_unavailable` over `busy`), `Retry-After: 1` only with `busy`; a retry only does the rest (TC-0237); ticked 2026-11-13: control audio-delete.test.ts (`busy and retry`, catalog order) and audio-routes.test.ts (the 200 body, 503 with `busy` and `Retry-After: 1`, `store_unsafe` and `audit_unavailable` without it, the retry; an all-`gone` outcome is a normal 200 `deleted: 0` with a `gone` list) and audio-delete.e2e.test.ts (two identities, one held; delete racing the sweep is 503 `busy`, never 409). The unsafe recheck: audio-catalog.test.ts (`recheckIdentity`: belongs, gone, unsafe), audio-delete.test.ts (`a recheck that cannot tell is pending store_unsafe, never gone`: a root made group-writable after `find`, the folder replaced by a link to a valid copy, the path replaced by a file) and audio-routes.test.ts (`an identity whose folder can no longer be judged under the lock (a file in its place) is 503 store_unsafe, not gone`)

fail-closed index: a role index that is a link, another user's file, over the cap or unreadable is untrusted (a missing index or folder is a trusted empty one); replay and delete answer 503 `store_unsafe` for it, touch nothing and never fall through to another identity's copy (TC-0238); ticked 2026-11-13: control audio-catalog.test.ts (`readSegmentIndex`: trusted-empty for a missing file or folder, untrusted for a link, ENOTDIR, a foreign file, over the cap), audio-replay.test.ts (no fall-through, the second and third reads), audio-routes.test.ts and audio-delete.e2e.test.ts (a symlinked index is 503 `store_unsafe` for replay and delete, never the other identity's copy)

deleted-aware sweep: the sweep and delete share one per-identity try-lock mutex and the typed `acquireStoreLock`; a segment with a `deleted` line is not indexed, so its WAV is an orphan and a half-finished delete is repaired by the next sweep; the sweep's own `audio.deleted` shape is unchanged (TC-0239); ticked 2026-11-13: control store-lock.test.ts (`IdentityMutex`, `acquireStoreLock` results, the source scan of every acquirer), sweep.test.ts (a segment with a `deleted` line is an orphan; malformed marks do not count; an untrusted index removes nothing) and audio-delete.e2e.test.ts (one shared mutex through `startControl`; the sweep finishing a crash after the index write)

a deleted segment never plays again (replay and listing answer `audio_deleted` / `deleted`, 410 over HTTP) and nothing leaks: no audio byte, path, id or name in a response, log or audit line, and `audio.deleted` lines are rebuilt field by field (an extra key is never written) (TC-0240); ticked 2026-11-13: control audio-replay.test.ts and audio-routes.test.ts (410 `audio_deleted`, a replay racing a delete sends no byte), audio-catalog.test.ts (the listing says `deleted`), audit-log.test.ts (`lineOf` drops extra keys), audio-routes.test.ts (`nothing in any response, and nothing logged, contains a path`) and audio-delete.e2e.test.ts (the audit file holds one line with no text, path or audio field)

a real store, worker files and control API work end to end (list, delete by the role and session scopes end to end, with the participant scope covered by the route and unit tests; replay 410, the sweep finishing a crash after the audit and after the index write, two identities with one busy) and the mutation checks (audit before marks, the live check, the mutex, the deleted mark, the fail-closed reader, path containment) each fail a named test and are reverted (TC-0241); ticked 2026-11-13: control audio-delete.e2e.test.ts (13 tests, real worker store, real API, real audit and sweep; crashes injected through file permissions; delete by the role and session scopes end to end, the participant scope is proven by audio-routes.test.ts and audio-delete.test.ts, not end to end) and the nine mutation runs of the Task 9 report (six mutation kinds: audit before marks, the live check (three places), the mutex (and a second mutex in `main.ts`), the deleted mark, the fail-closed reader, path containment), each failing named tests and reverted; prior evidence, not re-run here; the path-containment mutation is killed by unit tests only (the swap needs in-process timing). The e2e covers the role and session scopes; the participant scope is covered by the route and unit tests

stories.title: As an admin, I want per-person facilitator accounts that I manage from the console, with each session owned by the facilitator who created it, so that a client rollout can add and remove people, keep each person's sessions private and stop a person's access at once.

acs.text: accounts and passwords on disk: passwords are stored only as salted scrypt hashes (the hash never contains the plain text, equal passwords hash differently; a temporary password is 16 characters from a 31-character alphabet without look-alikes); the shared safe JSON file and `FileAccountStore` refuse a symlink, a hard-linked file, a foreign owner, a file accessible to group or other, a corrupt, oversize or wrong-shape file (duplicate ids or logins) and never return an empty result for one, a missing file reads as null, and a failed rename leaves the old file (TC-0270); ticked 2026-11-13: control accounts.passwords.test.ts, accounts.safe-json-file.test.ts and accounts.store.test.ts

the default admin: a missing `accounts.json` is a first start that creates `admin` (active, must change, no expiry) with `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` (10 to 200 characters) or the default `ChangeMe-Admin-1`, once even under concurrent starts; a corrupt or unsafe file is refused and never replaced; a present file never gets a second default admin; `ADMIN_RESET=1` restores the default with a new epoch, logs a loud line at every start (never a password) and never reopens the legacy latch; control logs one line while the default admin still must change (TC-0271); ticked 2026-11-13: control accounts.service.test.ts (ensure_default_admin, concurrent_ensure_default_admin, admin_reset_logs_the_loud_line, missing_file_is_first_start_but_corrupt_file_is_refused, present_file_never_gets_a_second_default_admin, admin_reset_restores_default, default_admin_does_not_expire), config.test.ts and main.test.ts

sign-in and password rules: logins are trimmed and lower-cased; an unknown login, a wrong password and a revoked account are all refused after exactly one hash verification; a correct temporary password older than 72 hours (invited, or active after a reset) answers `expired` and only with the right password; a password change needs at least 10 characters different from the current one, clears must-change, activates an invited account, closes the legacy latch and makes the old epoch fail (TC-0272); ticked 2026-11-13: control accounts.service.test.ts (login_unknown_wrong_and_revoked_all_refused_with_one_verify_each, login_after_72h_is_expired_only_with_the_right_password, change_password_*)

account lifecycle: create returns the temporary password once and stores only the hash and closes the legacy latch; a duplicate login (case-insensitive) is a conflict; a name that cleans to empty is invalid (`cleanConsoleName` now lives in `@acr/events`); resend replaces the temporary password and the old one stops working; reset returns an active account to must-change; revoke bumps the epoch and refuses sign-in; the last active admin cannot be revoked; reinstate issues a new temporary password; a public account never carries a password (TC-0273); ticked 2026-11-13: control accounts.service.test.ts (create_*, resend_*, reset_*, revoke_*, reinstate_*, public_account_never_has_password) and packages/events display-name.test.ts

control account routes and settings behind the service token: login, check, password, list, create, resend, reset, revoke, reinstate and the legacy latch; a refused account answers 401 `account_refused`, distinct from the token's 401; `AccountError` maps to 404, 409, 409 and 400; bodies are validated and length-limited; an unusable accounts file answers a generic 500 with no detail; an issued answer carries the temporary password and a list never does; logs never hold a password or hash (TC-0274); ticked 2026-11-13: control api.accounts.test.ts, api.test.ts and config.test.ts

session owners: `session-owners.json` is a separate safe file (a corrupt or group-writable file is refused), `sessions.json` is byte-identical with and without an owner, a session records its creator as owner, the owner can be assigned or cleared through `PUT /sessions/:id/owner` (unknown session 404), and an owner survives stop, restart, resume and end (TC-0275); ticked 2026-11-13: control accounts.owners.test.ts and supervisor.owner.test.ts

web sign-in: a login and password set the sealed console cookie `{ accountId, epoch }` (also with no `FACILITATOR_SECRET`); a wrong login or password is one neutral 401 that is charged per address, per login and globally (the sixth wrong password for one login is throttled even from a fresh address, and the right one is blocked too: the accepted 60 s lockout trade-off); an expired temporary password says so only after the right password; an unreachable control service answers 502 and charges nothing; Origin and Fetch-Metadata checks stay; a valid cookie is never blocked by the address throttle; no password or secret in any response or log (TC-0276); ticked 2026-11-13: web console-accounts.login.test.ts

every console request, server page and open event stream re-checks the account against control, so a revoked, reset or password-changed cookie fails on the very next request and an open stream ends within one heartbeat (a revoke closes that account's streams at once); control unreachable answers 502 and keeps the cookie; a must-change account is refused on every route, page and stream except the password change and the sign-out; the console is enabled without `FACILITATOR_SECRET` (TC-0277); ticked 2026-11-13: web console-recheck.test.ts (guard rechecks on every request, must_change blocks, open_stream_ends_within_one_heartbeat_after_revoke, close_account_closes_that_accounts_streams, control_unreachable_answers_502_and_keeps_the_cookie, console_enabled_without_facilitator_secret)

password change route: reachable while the account must change, re-seals the cookie so the old cookie fails (the second tab gets 401), refuses a legacy cookie (403) and an anonymous caller (401), checks Origin and the body, tells a wrong current password (403, cookie kept, charged to the account and eventually throttled) from a revoked or stale account (401, cookie cleared), and answers 502 with the cookie kept when control cannot classify a refusal (TC-0278); ticked 2026-11-13: web console-accounts.login.test.ts (change_password_reseals_cookie_old_cookie_fails_two_tabs_second_gets_401 and the password-route tests)

ownership on every console route that takes a session id: a facilitator gets the same neutral 404 for another facilitator's session as for an unknown one (the route table lists every session route), a session with no owner is admin-only, the admin can use any session, a facilitator can use their own, the session lookup is made once per request, the list is filtered for a facilitator and not for an admin, create records the caller as owner, the owner route is admin-only (a facilitator gets 403) and rejects an unknown or revoked account, and the review name `by` is the server-built account slug (a body `by` is ignored) (TC-0279); ticked 2026-11-13: web console-ownership.test.ts (route table, 404 on every route, admin-only unowned, list filter, create owner, set_owner, account slug, review_by)

reassigning or clearing a session's owner ends the previous owner's open streams (only that session's streams); a failed assignment leaves streams open; a throw while closing streams does not fail the assignment (TC-0280); ticked 2026-11-13: web console-ownership.test.ts (reassigning_a_session_ends_its_open_streams, clearing_the_owner, a_failed_assignment, a_throw_while_closing, hub_close_session_ends_only_that_sessions_streams)

admin account routes in the web app: a facilitator and a legacy caller get 403 on every one; create returns the temporary password and a list never does; each action needs Origin and the request header; the last-admin revoke returns its conflict message; control failures map to statuses; `by` comes from the cookie, never the body; a revoke closes that account's streams; ids and bodies are validated before any control call; the admin routes are blocked while the admin must change (TC-0281); ticked 2026-11-13: web console-admin-accounts.test.ts

the sign-in and forced change-password screens: the sign-in form posts login and password, goes straight to the password page when must-change, shows the neutral refusal, the expired, throttled and unreachable messages in words, shows the shared-secret disclosure only while the legacy sign-in is allowed, and keeps no password in storage or a URL; the change form labels three fields with the minimum length as helper text, rejects a mismatch or a short password before any request, sends the current and new password once, goes to the console on success and keeps no password in storage or a URL (TC-0282); ticked 2026-11-13: web ConsoleLogin.test.tsx and ChangePasswordForm.test.tsx

the admin Facilitators screen: lists name, login and status and shows only the actions allowed for each status (resend, reset, revoke, reinstate), asks to confirm each (revoke says running sessions keep running and stay reachable by the admin only), can create a facilitator or an admin and needs a name and a login, shows the credentials once as inert text with Copy buttons, removes the password from the page on dismiss and after a remount (it is never in storage or a URL), says plainly what went wrong, disables buttons while pending, and offers Try again after a load failure; a non-admin never sees the Admin link or page (TC-0283); ticked 2026-11-13: web FacilitatorsPanel.test.tsx and CredentialsPanel.test.tsx; console-recheck.test.ts (non_admin_never_sees_the_admin_link_or_page)

the session list shows the owner and an Assign control for an admin only: it offers only active accounts and Unassigned, posts the chosen owner and refreshes, shows an owner whose account is revoked or invited (and lets the admin unassign it or give it to an active account), shows an unknown owner as `Unknown account`, and a shared-secret admin sees no Owner column, makes no accounts call and gets no alert (TC-0284); ticked 2026-11-13: web SessionList.owner.test.tsx

end to end with the real control service and web app: the default admin signs in, is forced to change the password, and the default is refused afterwards; the shared secret is refused once the latch closed; the admin creates two facilitators and their temporary passwords show once and not after a reload; a facilitator is forced to change it, creates a session, and the other facilitator gets 404 (the same as for an unknown session) on the session, its stream and the list; the admin sees the owner; a revoke ends the owner's page and open stream within 8 s and refuses every later request with the old cookie while the session keeps Running; the admin assigns the session to the other facilitator who then runs it (TC-0285); ticked 2026-11-13: web e2e accounts.spec.ts (the journey; 2 of 2 passed in the Task 10 report, 2026-11-13: prior evidence, the controller re-runs it with the gates)

no serious or critical Axe violations (WCAG 2 A, AA, 2.1 A, AA), in light and dark, on the forced password change (empty and with the short-password refusal), the admin screen (the list, the one-time credentials and the revoke dialog) and the session list's Owner column with its select; no horizontal scroll at 1280 and 400 px (TC-0286); ticked 2026-11-13: web e2e accounts.spec.ts (the Axe test; passed in the Task 10 report, 2026-11-13: prior evidence)

the legacy shared secret: it signs in while the latch is open (and fails closed with 502 when the latch cannot be read), is refused once the first password change or the first created account closed the latch, acts as an admin for sessions but gets 403 on every admin account route and cannot change a password through the account route, and a legacy cookie is refused on its next request once the latch closes (TC-0287); ticked 2026-11-13: web console-accounts.login.test.ts, console-recheck.test.ts (legacy_cookie_without_kind_works_only_while_the_latch_is_open), console-admin-accounts.test.ts (facilitator_and_legacy_get_403_on_every_admin_route), control api.accounts.test.ts (legacy_route_reports_the_latch) and accounts.service.test.ts (create_closes_legacy, change_password_clears_must_change_closes_legacy)

documented: `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` ("Facilitator accounts": the default password and its mitigations, the temporary password on screen, epoch revoke and the stream heartbeat, ownership, throttles and the 60 s lockout, file safety, deleting `accounts.json` as a reset, the legacy latch), `docs/ROLLBACK.md` ("US-0083": deploy control before web, `ADMIN_RESET`, no data step), README, `.env.example`, `CHANGELOG.md`, the client demo cue card and `demo-up.sh` (TC-0288); ticked 2026-11-13: the Task 11 documents pass and `npm run plan:test`

tasks.title: Add a typed transient/permanent error classification to the adapters and a bounded retry in the NPC agent and Game Master
tasks.notes: Found in a live demo run: about 4 of 10 calls to a free OpenRouter model failed within 0.4 s with 'Upstream error from Nvidia: Service temporarily overloaded' and each became the canned fallback line. Delivered as ModelProviderError classification in the adapters, RetryingModelProvider, MODEL_MAX_RETRIES / MODEL_RETRY_BASE_MS, and attempt count plus kind in the NPC and GM alerts. The Game Master call now has its own deadline of max(NPC_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS, 60 s) and retries stop at it; the wait per retry is the backoff (base x 2^(n-1), +/-25%, capped at 4 s or the base) or a Retry-After up to 10 s, so the worst case is the attempts times 10 s, cut by the deadline. The Anthropic SDK's own retries are off when the provider is wrapped.

lessons.title: PlanVisualizer installs are additive; install only from the released main
lessons.rule:
Install PlanVisualizer only from a fresh clone of the released `main` branch, never from a local `develop` checkout. `install.sh` copies files but never deletes them, so installing over a different-version install leaves orphaned tools and tests that fail against the new version. When reinstalling, restore your own `AGENTS.md`, `plan-visualizer.config.json` and docs afterwards; the installer replaces a missing `AGENTS.md` with a 7-line stub and resets the config project name.
_Learned when a develop-era install (repository layer needing `proper-lockfile` and `better-sqlite3`) was overwritten by `main` v2.4.0 and 47 test suites failed on 189 leftover files._

lessons.title: Tests must pass on Linux and must not depend on timing
lessons.rule:
CI runs Ubuntu. Never put `/proc`, macOS-only paths, `stat -f`, fixed sleeps, small real timers (`setTimeout(50)`), wall-clock windows or the shared `/tmp` in a test. Inject clocks, delays and hooks so tests control ORDER; give slow real-process tests an explicit generous timeout; run new filesystem, lock and process tests once in a `node:22` container (root and non-root) before pushing.
_Learned when a test using `/proc/nope/trace.jsonl` hung the whole Workspace Tests job for 20 minutes on Linux (creating a directory in procfs hangs) while it passed instantly on macOS, and a 50 ms re-check test failed only on a loaded runner._

lessons.title: Open once and fstat the descriptor: never check a path and then use it
lessons.rule:
Do not `stat`, `lstat` or `exists` a path and then open or read the same path. Open the file once (`O_EXCL` or `O_NOFOLLOW` where relevant), then take type, size, link count and mode from `fstat` on that descriptor. Tests too: read through one descriptor.
_Learned when CodeQL `js/file-system-race` (high) blocked pull requests six times on the demo audit, the Game Master trace writer, the report reader and their tests._

lessons.title: Never log an environment-derived string
lessons.rule:
Log constants, port numbers and booleans, never a value that came from an environment variable (bind host, paths, origins, tokens). Say 'bound to loopback only', not the address. Error messages for an invalid setting name the variable, not its value.
_Learned when CodeQL `js/clear-text-logging` (high) flagged the startup log line `runtime listening on ws://<host>` and an earlier `custom endpoint` log twice._

lessons.title: Pin the identity you compare: Linux reuses inode numbers at once
lessons.rule:
A lock or file identity check by device and inode is only sound while the file stays open. Hold the judged file descriptor open through the whole takeover so the inode cannot be recycled, and test the ORDER of a takeover race with injected hooks, not with timers.
_Learned when a stale-lock takeover closed the judged file first; on Linux the freed inode number was reused by the new holder's lock, the identity check matched a live lock and removed it, which could let two servers share one log. macOS did not show it._

lessons.title: Authenticate any model output that triggers an irreversible state change
lessons.rule:
The Game Master's `true` ends a scene, so a verdict must carry a per-evaluation secret nonce that exists only in the system prompt, and the parser must reject quoted, echoed, nested, duplicated, array, truncated and conflicting verdicts. 'Last JSON object wins' and a plain-text fallback are injectable by a participant typing `verdict: true`.
_Learned when an independent review reproduced five ways a tolerant parser returned a false `true` from participant text._

lessons.title: A write that fails part-way must fail-stop, not retry into divergent state
lessons.rule:
After any failure once writing has started (write, `fdatasync`, lock check) mark the log permanently broken, halt the engine, tell clients with an unlogged notice and exit non-zero for a supervisor. The log is the source of truth on restart. Check that every append path honours the flag, and that multi-append operations are completed on resume.
_Learned when a failed `fdatasync` left an event on disk that the engine never applied, and every later tick appended another `scene.exited` forever; a crash between two appends left a resumed session stuck with no scene._

lessons.title: Independent review with probes finds what tests and the author miss
lessons.rule:
Keep the build-then-review loop. Give the reviewer the diff, the requirement, and permission to run probes in a scratch copy. Re-review risky fixes (a fix introduced a CPU-amplification bug and a data-loss window). Exhaustive tests (cut a log at every event boundary) beat sampled ones.
_Learned when every Critical and Important finding on this project (forged verdicts, aborted re-ask, post-refusal frames, log divergence, crash windows) was reproduced by running code rather than found by reading._

lessons.title: Real model runs find what mock runs cannot
lessons.rule:
A green mock demo says nothing about prompt behaviour. After changing a prompt, parser or scenario script, run the live showcase on the real model and read the transcript.
_Learned when the private 'intent' text leaked after a `***` separator into every generated player line, characters spoke for each other, the CFO echoed the sponsor and replies were truncated by a too-small token budget: all invisible in mock mode and all found only in live transcripts._

lessons.title: Reserve id blocks for parallel work and keep generated files out of hand merges
lessons.rule:
When stories are built in parallel, reserve disjoint id blocks in the registry first, tell implementers not to edit the registry or `docs/plan-status.*`, and reconcile at merge; regenerate dashboards with `npm run plan:generate` instead of merging them. Also: parallel agents share `/tmp`, so tests that count temp directories flake.
_Learned when three parallel branches all appended to the same plan, registry and changelog sections; reserved blocks kept the ids unique and only text conflicts remained._

lessons.title: Never paste a secret into a chat or a repository file
lessons.rule:
Do not paste API keys into chat; put them in the git-ignored `.env` yourself. Redact secrets in any log written to the repository (the prompt log) and scan the output before committing. Rotate any key that was exposed and record the incident in `progress.md`.
_Learned when an OpenRouter key was pasted into a prompt on 2026-10-02; it stayed out of every committed file but must be rotated._

lessons.title: Never pass an async function where a synchronous check is expected
lessons.rule:
A guard or pre-commit hook typed `() => void` silently accepts an `async` function in TypeScript, so the check never runs and a rejection goes unhandled. Type such hooks as `() => undefined` (or reject a returned promise at run time and attach a catch), use the synchronous check (`lock.lost || !lock.verify()`) for file operations, and grep every use of an `async` function in a void-callback position.
_Learned when `lock.assertHeld()` (async) was used as a synchronous pre-rename check in the join-code file: the lock was never actually checked, a lost lock still committed or deleted the file, and the rejected promise would have crashed Node 22. Two review passes caught it only by running a probe._

lessons.title: Secrets shown once must survive a failed start
lessons.rule:
If a value is persisted before it is shown to the operator (join codes, tokens), every failure path between the write and the display must undo the write, and a start with nothing recorded yet must issue and show new values instead of silently keeping unseen ones. Test it: make the start fail, restart, and assert the value is shown.
_Learned when a port in use, a missing API key or a bad trace-file path left join codes on disk that nobody had seen, so the next start kept them silently and no player could join._

lessons.title: An abort must wait for the work it cancelled, and every resource is owned from the moment it exists
lessons.rule:
A timeout or abort that reports and returns without waiting for the work it cancelled leaks whatever that work creates next (temp directories, servers, files) and lets it keep running after the result is out. After aborting, wait for the work to unwind with a bounded grace, then clean up; hand each resource to the cleanup list the moment it exists (right after `mkdtemp`, not after it is filled) and have the code that makes it remove it if it is aborted half-way; check the abort signal after each await on the start-up path. Test abort paths deterministically: inject the timer and fire it by hand at the exact point (a hook between creation and registration), never with a small real timeout.
_Learned when the demo watchdog test failed intermittently under coverage (BUG-0007): the 100 ms watchdog fired while the run's temp directory was being made, `runDemo` returned, and the directory was registered and removed fire-and-forget later, or recreated by the run that was still going._

lessons.title: Review ground-truth data against the rubric, not only the schema
lessons.rule:
When data is the oracle (calibration probes, golden files, expected scores), have a reviewer judge each item against the rule that defines it (the rubric's own level anchors and its "choose the lower level when the higher anchor's key behaviour is missing" rule) and ask whether a careful rater could defend a different answer. A file that loads and validates can still carry a wrong label, and a wrong label silently biases every metric computed from it (bias, exact agreement, tuning).
_Learned when two starter probes labelled "level 4" for negotiation validated, passed every test and were level 3 by the rubric's anchor (no recommendation, no held condition, no stated-back next steps); only the content review caught it._

lessons.title: A quality label must require its headline measure, and a fix can create the next hole
lessons.rule:
If a label (PASS/WARN/FAIL) is supposed to certify a property, make the label impossible to earn without measuring that property: a rule that is silently skipped when its inputs are missing (no contrast probes, all answers unusable) turns "not measured" into "passed". After closing such a hole, re-test the neighbouring failure modes: the first fix made an outage read as a flat judge, and the second made a mid-run failure replace a good result. Give every rule a test for "no data", "partial data" and "all data bad".
_Learned when the calibration label let a judge that answered 3 to everything PASS (no contrast probes, or every contrast probe unusable), then labelled an outage as a flat judge, then let a judge that died mid-run replace a good summary file._

lessons.title: CodeQL scans test files, and a failed run must never overwrite the last good result
lessons.rule:
(1) In tests as well as production code, never check a path and then use it (`stat`/`lstat`/`access`/`exists` then `open`/`read`/`stat` of the same path): open once and read the mode and contents from that file handle; never assert HTML escaping with a regexp that filters tags: use substring checks. (2) A command that writes a "latest result" file that other tools read (a calibration summary the report stamp trusts) must replace it only after a complete, healthy run; a failed, aborted, partial or degraded run writes its own dated output and leaves the old file untouched.
_Learned when PR #36 failed the CodeQL check with three high alerts in a test file, and when review reproduced that an outage, a Ctrl-C, `--only` and a mid-run judge failure each replaced a good summary._

lessons.title: Verify that a captured artifact belongs to the run before you keep it
lessons.rule:
When you copy a log, transcript or result out of a temporary location, check that it is from the run you mean: timestamps inside it, the scenario id and version, the model names. Do not assume that the newest or only matching directory is yours. Name the location a tool really writes to (the live showcase writes `$TMPDIR/acr-showcase-run-XXXX/data/demo.jsonl`), set `TMPDIR` to a known folder for the run, and copy from there.
_Learned when a copy loop synced `acr-demo-*` directories (another demo mode) and saved a stale mock-story session log as if it were a live run's log; it was caught only by reading the timestamps and scenario version in it._

lessons.title: When practice has an exception, the rule text must name the exception and its record
lessons.rule:
If a written rule says "an agent never does X" and an agent does X on explicit owner instruction, change the rule the same day to say who may do it, under what instruction, and where the record lives (here: `approve` may be run by an agent only on the owner's explicit instruction naming the items, and the approval is recorded in `approved_by`, the commit history and the docs Limits section). Otherwise the docs describe something that is no longer true and the next reader cannot tell a sanctioned exception from a breach.
_Learned when the `approve` help and docs said an agent never approves probes while an agent approved 26 probes on the owner's chat instruction of 2026-10-08; the rule was reworded and the Limits section now lists the approval records._

lessons.title: A test double of a platform API must copy the platform's dispatch rules
lessons.rule:
When a fake stands in for a browser or runtime API (EventSource, WebSocket, fetch), make it behave as the specification does in the cases the code branches on, and write one test that pins each such rule on the fake itself. A fake that is simpler than the platform hides exactly the bugs that live in the difference. Where the real thing is cheap to run (a real runtime in mock mode, Chromium under Playwright), run the same scenario against it as well.
_Learned when the web client's fake EventSource never called `onerror` for a server-sent `event: error` frame, while browsers do: every jsdom test passed and the real page would have shown a Reconnecting banner that never cleared on a healthy stream. Only an independent review caught it (Task 14 of slice 2a)._

lessons.title: Find where a framework buffers a request body before trusting your own size cap
lessons.rule:
A size cap in a route handler protects nothing if a layer before it (middleware, a proxy, a body parser) has already read the whole body into memory. For every new HTTP entry point, check which layers see the body and their limits, keep middleware off routes that do not need it, set the framework's own body limit, and test with an oversized request against the built server, not only the handler.
_Learned when Next 16 copied up to 10 MB of every POST into memory for the request proxy (`src/proxy.ts`) before the BFF's 8 KiB cap ran; the fix excluded `/api` from the proxy matcher and set `proxyClientMaxBodySize`, and a 12 MB POST to the built app was then refused without buffering._

lessons.title: The order frames arrive at a client is not the order the server decided
lessons.rule:
When a server decides an order (which of two joins is newer) and several client connections observe it, never infer that order from when each connection's frames were read: TCP reads of different sockets interleave arbitrarily, and a frame and its connection's close can arrive in one read. Carry the server's order explicitly (a counter, a sequence number) or wait for the authoritative signal (the close code), and reproduce the interleaving in a test with a proxy that holds and releases bytes.
_Learned when two browser tabs joining one seat could both end "superseded": the stream hub treated "the connection I heard from last" as the newest, and a delayed tab whose `joined` and 4001 close arrived together replaced the live tab. A holding TCP proxy in `hub.runtime.test.ts` reproduced it; one narrow ordering remains documented in the threat model._

lessons.title: A wait for "a frame that matches" must start after the trigger
lessons.rule:
When a test waits for a message that a trigger should cause, take the position in the inbox (or a counter) just before the trigger and wait only for messages after it. A predicate that an earlier message already satisfies makes the test pass with the feature removed. Prove each such test by deleting the behaviour once and seeing it fail.
_Learned when the roster tests waited for a roster frame with `f.next()` that matched the roster sent at join, so removing the consent, leave or disconnect broadcast still passed (Task 8 of slice 2a); the fix took an offset before each trigger and every broadcast was then proven by mutation._

lessons.title: Let the page settle before an accessibility scan measures it
lessons.rule:
Before Axe (or any check that reads computed colours or layout) runs, wait for a settled page: the state you mean to test is reached (the message shown, the control enabled, not busy) and `document.getAnimations()` has nothing running or pending. A colour transition that starts when the colour scheme changes leaves a half-way background beside text that switched at once, so a contrast check passes or fails depending on timing. Reproduce such a failure by slowing the transition (or the animation playback rate) in a scratch build, never by waiting longer.
_Learned when the first two CI runs of the web Axe spec failed in different places: once a button's contrast on the refused join screen right after switching from dark to light (its 0.12 s background transition was mid-way), once a line that never reached the transcript; a 3 s transition in a scratch build made the first failure happen every time, and waiting for the animations to finish fixed it._

lessons.title: Never append an event before the start: a non-empty log wedges `engine.start`
lessons.rule:
The engine refuses to start on a log that already holds an event (`log_not_empty`). Any code that runs before the session starts (a reissue, a roster change, an operator action) must keep its audit trail in memory or in a side file, never as a facilitator alert in the session log. Add a test that performs the action on a lobby and then starts the session.
_Learned when the first design of the parent-only code reissue appended a facilitator alert before the start; the review found that one pre-start reissue made the later `start` fail. Alerts are appended only after `session.started` (slice 2b-1, Task 9)._

lessons.title: A rollback that deletes files must first wait for the child to exit
lessons.rule:
When a supervisor rolls back a half-created child (failed start, timeout), kill it, await its exit (bounded by a timer), force-kill if it survives, and only then delete its files and free its slot. A dying process can still write a file after you removed it, and a freed slot lets a second create race the first child's lock. A child that survives SIGKILL keeps its slot reserved.
_Learned when the control service's rollback deleted the session files at once after `kill()`; the review showed a late write could resurrect them and the slot count could exceed `MAX_SESSIONS` (slice 2b-1, Task 11a; ruling R9)._

lessons.title: A fake child that exits synchronously hides shutdown races
lessons.rule:
In tests for process supervision, model `kill()`, `exit` and `message` asynchronously (a later tick), the way a real child behaves. A fake that emits `exit` inside `kill()` makes "await the exit" and "persist after the exit" look correct, and the same code then races against a real process. Back the unit tests with at least one test on a real forked child, and check a test is red against the old code.
_Learned when the first rollback test for the control service passed against code that did not wait for the child: its fake exited inside `kill()`. Fixed by writing the late file in `setImmediate` before the exit (slice 2b-1, Task 11a)._

lessons.title: A client-chosen id must never equal a server placeholder
lessons.rule:
If the server stores a placeholder value in a field the client also fills (for example `rebind-pending` in the consent file's participant id), refuse that value from every client path (the schema, `give`, `adopt`) and make `has()` false for it. Otherwise a client can claim the waiting state by naming it. Test each entry point with the placeholder itself.
_Learned when the consent rebind marker `rebind-pending` could be chosen as a participant id through `give`, `adopt` and the protocol schema, which would have let a joining client inherit a seat's consent (slice 2b-1, Task 9 review)._

lessons.title: A failed seat persist needs an in-memory rollback
lessons.rule:
When an operation changes in-memory state and then persists it (revoke a credential, release a consent), a failed persist must restore the memory too, in the same order it was changed. Otherwise the running process and the file disagree: a role can stay open to the old code, or the old holder is locked out for a change that was never saved. Make the failure test assert the in-memory state, not only that an error was thrown.
_Learned when a failed seat persist in the reissue left the role open to the OLD code and the consent released in memory, and the test only checked the error (slice 2b-1, Task 9 review). Remaining gap: the two-file persist (credentials, then consent) can still diverge on disk if the second write fails._

lessons.title: Repo-wide scanner tests run in one package and read all of them
lessons.rule:
Tests that walk the whole repository (`id-rules.files.test.ts`, `test-hygiene.test.ts` in `services/runtime`) apply to every package, including new ones, but a per-file container run of the new package does not execute them. Before closing a slice that adds a package or test files, run the full `pnpm test:coverage` (or those scanner files) and not only the recipe on the files you changed.
_Learned at the close of slice 2b-1: the scanners reported `services/control/src/api.ts:89` (an identifier-rule regex) and `services/control/src/__tests__/supervisor.real.test.ts:103` (an elapsed-time assertion) that sixteen task-level runs had not executed._

lessons.title: When events are broadcast as they are written, a flag set at the end of the operation must not refuse what the first event allows
lessons.rule:
If a multi-step operation broadcasts each event as it is persisted (start: `session.started`, the characters, `scene.entered`, the opening inject) but sets its "done" flag only after the last step, clients act on the early events while the flag is still false. A request they make in that window must wait for the operation in flight (and be refused only if it fails), not be refused by the flag. Test the window deterministically: hold the log's appends after the event the client acts on (a gated log), make the request, assert it is pending, then release; never rely on a slow disk or a sleep. When an E2E helper reports a refusal it should never see, look for this window on the server before blaming the test.
_Learned when the Web E2E on PR #60 got `409 not_started` for a say sent after the page showed the scene: the runtime set `started` only after writing the opening inject (BUG-0009, open since the first Web E2E run and seen there as a missing transcript line)._

lessons.title: A directory that a loader reads in full must hold only what the loader owns
lessons.rule:
The review loaders (`loadDrafts`, `siblingReleased`, `moderate open`) read every `*.json` and `*.md` in a review folder and refuse anything unknown. Never put another feature's file there, even a credential or index file that "belongs with the reports". Keep it in a sibling location (the report-access store is one `report-access.json` under `CONTROL_DATA_DIR`). When a design says "beside X", check what reads X's directory before choosing the path.
_Learned in the Opus review of the slice 2c-1 plan: a planned `access.json` inside `reports/<sessionId>/` would have made every later `moderate release` in that folder fail as corrupt (`review/draft.ts:334`, `review/store.ts:300`)._

lessons.title: A rate limit keyed on the address alone locks out a room behind one NAT
lessons.rule:
Workshops put many participants behind one public address. Count only failures per address (and block with a 429 and `Retry-After`, never the same text as a refused credential), and limit successful requests per credential or session instead. A refusal text that is also what a throttle returns hides the real cause from the person who is blocked.
_Learned in the final review of slice 2c-1 PR 2: the read route charged every read per address (60 a minute for the whole room), and a blocked enter looked like "Not found" to a participant with a valid link._

lessons.title: A "Reserved blocks" paragraph in the ID registry marks every id it names as used
lessons.rule:
`tests/unit/id-registry.test.js` reads every id that appears in a "Reserved blocks" paragraph of `docs/ID_REGISTRY.md` as already used, so the next-available row must be beyond all of them. Never write a BUG or L id (even in a sentence saying none are reserved) in such a paragraph; say "no new BUG or L ids are reserved" without the numbers, and move the Next Available row of a sequence only when you file the item.
_Learned in the slice 2c-4 plan: naming the next free BUG and L ids in the reservation paragraph made the registry test fail until the numbers were removed._

lessons.title: A test must wait for the event that makes its precondition true before it reads state
lessons.rule:
When a test takes a baseline (an inbox length, a log offset, a counter) and later asserts on what came after it, first wait for the event that makes the baseline final: the frame the subject's own action causes on the subject's own channel. Waiting on a different observer (a second socket) proves nothing about the first, because separate sockets are handled in no fixed order. A flake that appears only in whole-file or loaded runs and never in a single-test run is usually this race; reproduce it with a loop of whole-file runs before fixing, and verify the fix with at least twice as many.
_Learned when BUG-0026's roster test read `before` after the facilitator's frame but before the first connection's own join roster, so that roster was counted as a post-takeover frame (6 failures in 25 whole-file runs, none in 50 after the wait)._

lessons.title: Check the credential before charging an address throttle
lessons.rule:
When a request carries an authenticated credential (a sealed AES-GCM cookie, a signed token), verify it FIRST and send a valid one straight to its own per-credential budget; consult and charge the per-address failure throttle only when verification fails. A per-address block checked before the credential lets junk from one person behind a shared address (a workshop NAT) lock out every valid holder behind it, and protects nothing, because a forger cannot produce a credential that verifies. Keep each failure class in its own throttle table, so a flood of one kind cannot saturate the table another route needs.
_Learned in BUG-0025: the report read and write routes checked the address block before unsealing the cookie, in the same table as the enter route, so forged cookies could answer 429 to valid readers and, once the table was saturated, to valid enters._

lessons.title: After a realtime reconnect, ask again for what you subscribed to, and never wait for ever on the server's answer
lessons.rule:
A subscription is state on the server; a full reconnect can drop it without any event telling you. Keep the set of things you want, re-request each one that has no delivered track when the connection reports `Reconnected`, and bound every wait for a subscription (or any other server answer) with an injected timer, so a request the server silently drops ends in a bounded retry or a visible failure instead of a component that looks healthy and hears nothing.
_Learned in the A1b live checks (US-0071, D59 and D60): after a full reconnect rtc-node never answered the re-subscribe sent while reconnecting (4 frames in 60 s), and a refused subscription was never answered either, so a read waited for ever; one plain re-request after `Reconnected` brought the audio back, and a 10 s `SUBSCRIBE_WAIT_MS` now ends a read nobody answers._

lessons.title: Attribute buffered data by the generation that produced it, checked per item, not by the channel it arrives on
lessons.rule:
When a channel (a seat, a role, a socket slot) can change owner while data from the old owner is still buffered, unsubscribing is not enough: frames already queued keep arriving. Tag each item at its source with an owner generation and drop it at the consumer when the generation is no longer current, item by item. Closing the old stream early is defence in depth; the per-item check is the guarantee, and a race test with the check mutated away must fail.
_Learned in A1b (US-0071, review finding behind Task 7): rtc-node's `AudioStreamSource.teardown` keeps already-buffered frames readable after `setSubscribed(false)`, so a reissued seat would have recorded the old holder's last words under the new holder's name without the generation check in `TrackPipeline`._

lessons.title: A fake must hang where the real thing hangs
lessons.rule:
A test double that settles a pending read, a `return()` or a request at once hides every hang the real library has. Model the real ordering in the fake (a `return()` queued behind a pending `next()`, an unsubscribe that takes effect late, an answer that never comes) and keep a test that proves the code survives it; a component excluded from coverage because it wraps the real library needs a live check that exercises it directly.
_Learned in A1b (US-0071, batch 3 review F11 and the live checks): the fake room settled a pending `next()` on `return()` and answered every subscribe, so a deaf seat after a dropped stream and a read that waited for ever passed every unit test and showed up only against a real LiveKit server._

lessons.title: Never hang state on a rate-limited or deferred alert path
lessons.rule:
An alert path that is rate limited, or kept until later (before a session starts), drops or delays messages by design. Anything that changes behaviour (availability, voice off, a mute) needs its own message, applied first, with no rate limit and also before the start; the alert then only informs a human.
_Learned in the A1b plan review (US-0071, K7 and R23): Whisper being unhealthy was going to ride the `stt_unavailable` alert, which the runtime limits to one per 30 s and keeps unraised before the start, so a page could have kept saying "recording" while nothing was transcribed; `voice_availability` became a separate parent message._

lessons.title: Read the installed library source before trusting what its documentation implies
lessons.rule:
For any behaviour a security or privacy property depends on (what a mute does, what a 404 means, where a logger lives), read the pinned version's installed source and pin the answer with a test. Documentation and method names describe intent, not the edge cases.
_Learned in A1b (US-0071): livekit-client 2.23.0's `setMicrophoneEnabled(false)` only mutes the published track (D40: the page now unpublishes it); rtc-node 1.2.1's logger is not exported and logs identities at debug level (D10: silenced by file path); `livekit-server-sdk` maps a non-JSON 404 to a twirp error with no code, so "any 404 is not found" made removals silent no-ops against the wrong server (batch 2 F1)._

lessons.title: A package script must never share a name with a package-manager built-in
lessons.rule:
Before naming a script that a root script hands over to (`pnpm --filter <pkg> <name>`), run `pnpm help <name>`: pnpm resolves a built-in (or its alias) before a script of the same name. Give the script a name no built-in has, and write `run` explicitly in every handing-over root script; pin both with a test that reads `package.json`.
_Learned in the A1c plan review (US-0072, K13): `pnpm -s --filter @acr/voice-ops up` would have run `pnpm update` (its alias `up`) in that package and rewritten its `package.json` and the lockfile, instead of starting voice. The scripts became `voice-up` and friends, called with `run`._

lessons.title: `fetch` and Node's global agent follow an environment proxy: probes that carry a secret use `node:http` with `agent: false`
lessons.rule:
With `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` (Node 22.21 and later) global `fetch` and the default `http` agent send requests, the full URL included, to `HTTP_PROXY`. Any request whose URL or headers carry a secret (a secret request path, an admin token) goes through `node:http` with `agent: false`, to a literal loopback address only, and a test runs it in a child Node started with the proxy variables set (Node reads them at start-up) with the child's own default-agent request as the proof that the proxy was live.
_Learned in A1c (US-0072, review A F10 and review B F2): the `STT_URL` path and the LiveKit admin token would have reached a proxy; the first test set the variables at run time and so proved nothing._
